questions.stem: Which is the oldest National Park in India, established in 1936?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett NP (Uttarakhand) was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park — India's first — renamed in 1957 after the famous hunter-conservationist Jim Corbett. It is also where Project Tiger was launched in 1973. Spread over 520 sq km in the Nainital district. Known for its high density of Bengal tigers, Indian elephants, gharials in the Ramganga river.

questions.stem: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is located in which state and is inscribed on which UNESCO list?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga NP (Assam) was inscribed as a UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site in 1985. Home to two-thirds of the world's population of Indian one-horned rhinoceroses (Rhinoceros unicornis). It hosts the 'Big Five' of Kaziranga: one-horned rhino, Bengal tiger, Asian elephant, wild water buffalo, and swamp deer (eastern barasingha). Also a tiger reserve (2006) and Important Bird Area. Spans floodplains of the Brahmaputra.

questions.stem: Namdapha National Park, India's fourth largest NP and home to four species of big cats (Tiger, Leopard, Clouded Leopard, Snow Leopard), is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Namdapha NP (Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh) is the 4th largest NP in India (1985 sq km) and the northernmost lowland evergreen rainforest in the world. Unique distinction: it is the ONLY park in the world where all four big cat species coexist — Bengal tiger, common leopard, clouded leopard, and snow leopard. Also home to red panda, hoolock gibbon (India's only ape), and the recently discovered Namdapha flying squirrel.

questions.stem: Which National Park is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica)?
questions.explanation: Gir NP (Junagadh, Gujarat) is the ONLY place in the world where the Asiatic Lion survives in the wild, after having once been on the verge of extinction (only 20 lions in 1913). Current population ~674 (2020 census); projected higher in 2025 census. Historically lived from Syria to Bengal. Gir also houses leopards, chinkara, chausingha (four-horned antelope), pangolin, and 300+ bird species. Adjacent Barda and Mitiyala sanctuaries serve as extended habitat.

questions.stem: Sundarbans, home to the Royal Bengal Tiger and one of the largest mangrove forests in the world, is located at the delta of which rivers?
questions.explanation: Sundarbans NP (West Bengal) covers the Indian part of the Sundarbans delta formed by the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers meeting the Bay of Bengal. It is: (a) UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987), (b) a Biosphere Reserve (1989), (c) a Tiger Reserve, (d) a Ramsar wetland (2019). Known for the 'swimming tigers' of Sundarbans — the local Bengal tigers are excellent swimmers, adapted to tidal waters. Habitat for saltwater crocodile, king cobra, Gangetic dolphin.

questions.stem: Which of the following was the FIRST Biosphere Reserve established in India (1986)?
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (TN/Karnataka/Kerala tri-junction) was established in 1986 — India's FIRST of 18 biosphere reserves. It covers Mudumalai, Bandipur, Nagarhole, Wayanad, Mukurthi, Silent Valley. Of the 18 Indian BRs, 12 are recognised under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme. The Gulf of Mannar was the first marine biosphere reserve. Kachchh is the largest by area; Nokrek (Meghalaya) is the smallest.

questions.stem: Which was the FIRST Ramsar wetland designated in India in 1981?
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake (Odisha — largest brackish-water lagoon in Asia) and Keoladeo NP (Rajasthan — formerly Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary) were BOTH designated as India's first Ramsar sites on 1 October 1981. As of 2024, India has 85+ Ramsar sites — the highest in Asia (Tamil Nadu leads with ~16 sites). The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (1971, Iran) aims to conserve wetlands of international importance. World Wetlands Day: 2 February.

questions.stem: Kuno National Park, where cheetahs were reintroduced to India in September 2022 after 70 years of extinction, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Kuno NP (Sheopur district, Madhya Pradesh) saw the arrival of 8 cheetahs from Namibia on 17 Sept 2022 (PM Modi's birthday) under 'Project Cheetah' — the world's first inter-continental cheetah translocation. A second batch of 12 came from South Africa in Feb 2023. Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952 (last one in Chhattisgarh's Koriya district). MP is sometimes called India's 'Tiger State' but is now also its 'Cheetah State'. Kuno was earlier developed as an alternative lion habitat.

questions.stem: Which Indian state has the highest number of National Parks (11)?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has the MOST national parks (11): Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Satpura, Panna, Madhav, Van Vihar, Sanjay (Dubri), Kuno, Fossil (Mandla), Dinosaur Fossil (Dhar). MP is also called the 'Tiger State' based on tiger numbers (785 tigers per 2022 census — highest in India). Andhra Pradesh + Telangana together have 6. Maharashtra has 6. Uttarakhand 6. Karnataka 5. Kerala 6.

questions.stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in which year and from which National Park?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 from Jim Corbett NP during Indira Gandhi's premiership, in response to alarming tiger declines (India had ~40,000 tigers in 1900, dropped to ~1,827 by 1972). Initially 9 tiger reserves; now 54 (most recent: Kaudia TR in UP in 2024). NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority) is the statutory body under Wildlife Protection Act (2006 amendment). 2022 census: 3,682 tigers (up from 2,967 in 2018) — India has ~75% of the world's wild tigers.

questions.stem: Which National Park is known as the 'Valley of Flowers', a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: Valley of Flowers NP (Chamoli district, Uttarakhand) was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005 and combines with the adjacent Nanda Devi NP for joint WHS status. The valley bursts into bloom during the short summer (July-September) with 600+ flower species — including the blue Himalayan poppy (Meconopsis), cobra lily, saussurea, orchids. British mountaineer Frank Smythe stumbled upon it in 1931 and wrote 'The Valley of Flowers' (1938). Also mentioned in the Ramayana as the place where Hanuman fetched the Sanjeevani herb for Lakshmana.
